title: p11scope observed-profile v3 document
description: Consumer aid for live v3 profile and v3-metrics documents (SYSPLAN residual F-50). The evidence object is closed per lane; the release oracle (scripts/check-capture-evidence.py) is the enforcement behind this file, and tests/python/test_schema_json.py keeps the two in agreement. Terminal trace EVIDENCE objects are not documents and are out of scope, as are historical v2 shapes.

caller.description: Pid-scope target identity, present only for pid scope with resolved caller identity: exactly one of exe/exe_unknown_reason is non-null.

counter_collection.description: Optional availability of the accepted cumulative counter snapshot. Cached ticks retain its original read window; failed attempts retain its mode and generation.

bank_gaps.description: Optional per-bank gap disclosure, present only when the acquisition was partial.

scope.const: D-transitive depth=2 objects<=32 edges<=128 exe-bytes<=1MiB capture-bytes<=64MiB names<=255B verdicts<=1024

legacy_collection.description: Optional legacy gap disclosure, present only when the legacy aggregate read was partial.

detach_event_loss.description: EVENTS ring losses accrued after the capture loop ended through the terminal snapshot (the quiesce + terminal-drain window): the terminal reading minus the loop-end reading. Excludes anything lost during or after the post-publication producer detach.

detach_discovery_loss.description: Discovery-ring losses accrued after the capture loop ended through the terminal snapshot (the quiesce + terminal-drain window): the terminal reading minus the loop-end reading. Excludes anything lost during or after the post-publication producer detach.

discovery_deferrals.description: Live discovery frames that spent their work budget and deferred the rest of their discovery work, in order, to the next frame. A scheduling fact, never a loss; work still undone after the terminal drain is published as a loss instead.

stage_unknown_clock.description: Stage spans dropped for a failed clock read; in no total.

tail_skips.description: Batch-tail publications skipped as provably redundant.

detach.description: Wall time of producer-detach work completed before publication, in whole milliseconds. The terminal callback publishes before the producers detach (quiesce-then-publish, so the report never waits on link teardown), so Detailed reports carry 0 here: post-publication teardown is explicitly unmeasured in the report, by design.

attach_mono_ns.description: Authoritative CLOCK_MONOTONIC reading when the session became fully attached, or null when the capture never reached its loop.

loop_start_mono_ns.description: Authoritative CLOCK_MONOTONIC reading at the first capture-loop tick, or null when the loop never started.

loop_end_mono_ns.description: Authoritative CLOCK_MONOTONIC reading when the capture loop ended, or null when the loop never ended.

stage_ms.description: Per-stage wall time in whole milliseconds, cumulative leaf-span sums (a different clock from phase_ms; no identity between them).

longest_op.description: The capture's longest single recorded span; all null when none was recorded.

inter_drain_gap.description: Bounded inter-drain gap distribution; quantiles are bucket upper bounds, max is exact.

newcomer_queue.description: Newcomer/refresh queue ages in whole milliseconds.

max_rss_kb.description: Maximum periodic RSS in KiB. It includes the EVENTS ring's double user mapping (about twice the ring size, about 64 MiB at the 32M default), which is not extra memory: the ring is charged once as locked kernel memory.

scope.const: D-transitive depth=2 objects<=32 edges<=128 exe-bytes<=1MiB capture-bytes<=64MiB names<=255B verdicts<=1024

selected_detail.description: Optional additive 6.15 endpoint-selection envelope (--select-endpoint beside counter captures). Closed nested shape; the release oracle is the enforcement behind this file. Never carries process identity.

latency_ns.description: Timing availability from the measured counter capability. Null is unmeasured; numeric zero remains a measured value.

initialization.description: Optional v3-additive Initialize claim, present only on rows that name C_Initialize with at least one positively counted return. The outcome class over the row's own completed calls; potential_provider is a true-only likelihood, never proof. Absent means Initialize was not observed on this row.

rv_names.description: V3-additive CKR_* names for the rv_counts keys that have a registered name, keyed by the same 16-digit hex strings. Unregistered (vendor) codes are absent; their rv_counts hex key is the verbatim rendering. Render-time presentation of already-captured return codes; rv_counts is unchanged.

ring_account.description: One ring's cross-check account: kernel submitted (produced) and refused (dropped) totals against the userspace drained (consumed) total and the queued remainder. still_queued/unexplained are absent exactly when the remainder is structurally unknowable (a live EVENTS ring).

resource_sample.description: One capture-process resource sample; every field is null when its read or parse failed.

utime_ms.description: User CPU time in whole milliseconds, from /proc/self/stat.

stime_ms.description: System CPU time in whole milliseconds, from /proc/self/stat.

read_bytes.description: Storage bytes read (the read_bytes key), from /proc/self/io.

write_bytes.description: Storage bytes written (the write_bytes key), from /proc/self/io.

selected_detail_rv_counts.description: Return-value rows keyed by the canonical decimal u64 the collector renders; possibly empty.
